subject: Subprocessor onboarding: evidence catalog and dataflow clarifications
messages:
From: Jen Park <security@medicorp.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: tim.rogers@medicorp.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Request: updated subprocessor inventory + CAIQ mappings

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking our call this morning. As part of our vendor tender we need a current subprocessor inventory and a short evidence bundle to validate supply-chain controls:

- CSV of active subprocessors (name, service, region, data types processed, start date, contractual status)
- Evidence that cryptographic keys for customer data are under KMS/HSM controls (certificate or attest)
- CAIQ pointers for network segmentation and ingress controls (page/section references are OK)
- Recent SOC 2 Type II report or a link to download

Could you turn these around by EOD Monday (Dec 7) so the procurement team can proceed with the security gating? If there are any subprocessors with EU data residency implications please flag them.

Best,
Jen Park
Head of Vendor Security, MediCorp

Attachment: example_evidence_list_template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Jen Park <security@medicorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessor inventory + CAIQ mappings

Hi Jen — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you requested. Quick clarifications before I assemble the bundle:

1) By "CAIQ pointers" do you want full CAIQ answers (spreadsheet) or just references to our public security docs where we map each control? We can do either; references are faster.
2) For KMS/HSM evidence, we can provide a redacted attestation from our KMS provider plus the public key fingerprint and an internal control summary — is that sufficient?
3) Any particular sensitivity around subprocessors that process PHI vs general PII? We will flag PHI-handling subprocessors.

Action plan: I will attach the subprocessor CSV and a dataflow mapping PDF. Marissa will add the SOC 2 link and KMS attestation; Karthik will review EU residency flags. Expect a consolidated bundle by Monday EOD PST.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Partner Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_2026-12.csv (CSV)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: updated subprocessor inventory + CAIQ mappings

Rachel — looping Sergio (legal) and Karthik (privacy) so we can validate contractual status and residency flags before sending. Draft evidence I'm preparing:

- SOC 2 Type II (redacted) PDF and downloadable link (no sensitive customer data)
- KMS attestation (redacted) + key IDs
- CAIQ answer set for common sections (Network, Cryptography, Logging) as pointers to our security playbook
- Dataflow mapping (customer data lanes highlighted)

Sergio: do we need to run the CSV through legal review for any DO NOT DISCLOSE items?

Thanks — I'll drop the doc links here once uploaded.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal, Compliance Programs

Attachment: dataflow_mapping_v3.pdf (PDF)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 10:56:00 -0800

All good. A couple of legal notes before external delivery:

- Remove internal ticket IDs from the CSV and strip any internal contact emails that are not vendor-facing.
- Replace exact start-dates with month/year for subprocessors we treat as confidential per vendor agreements.
- For any subprocessor that supports regulated PHI-handling, add a short note referencing the data processing addendum section number.

Rachel, once Marissa uploads the bundle to our secure Share link, I will sign off. We should include a short cover email that enumerates the artifacts (so their procurement can track).

Sergio Alvarez
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@cleardata.io>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Jen Park <security@medicorp.com>, tim.rogers@medicorp.com
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor onboarding: evidence catalog and dataflow clarifications

Hi Rachel — thanks to you and the team for the fast turnaround. We received the secure Share link and pulled the bundle. Confirmations below:

- redwood_subprocessor_inventory_2026-12.csv received and validated against MediCorp's vendor schema. We asked for month/year only on start date and redacted internal contacts — confirmed.
- dataflow_mapping_v3.pdf is clear; PHI-processing lanes are highlighted and labeled.
- SOC2-TypeII-2026-cert.pdf link works and certificate metadata matches the date range MediCorp requires.
- KMS attestation (redacted) included key IDs and indicated HSM-backed KMS in use — acceptable.

Procurement will open the security gate and proceed with the PO next week. We might ask a follow-up about ourinternal-logging retention policy (how long unredacted logs are kept) — if so, we'll ping you.

Thanks again,
Asha Patel
Vendor Risk Analyst, ClearData (on behalf of MediCorp)
